article_title: Effect of simulator fidelity on skill acquisition and trainee satisfaction in arthroscopic surgery training for novices: a prospective randomized comparative study.
citation: Kutsuna Tatsuhiko, Kinoshita Tomofumi, Hino Kazunori, Watamori Kunihiko, Tsuda Takashi, Yamaoka Shintaro, Takao Masaki. (2025). Effect of simulator fidelity on skill acquisition and trainee satisfaction in arthroscopic surgery training for novices: a prospective randomized comparative study. International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11548-025-03528-5
title: AZBOTS low-fidelity benchtop arthroscopy simulator with eight task boxes
description: The AZBOTS simulator (Marui & Co., Ltd.) is "a low-fidelity device developed for training surgeons in various arthroscopic procedures". It contains 8 task boxes covering inspection, touching, loose-body removal, size estimation, cutting, pinch-and-connection, going over the line, and pinch-and-pulling, using actual surgical instruments. Training is guided by time limits and auditory error alarms, with completion scores displayed after each task. In the study, AZBOTS participants completed the 8 task boxes sequentially for 90 minutes, practicing inspection, instrument handling, and object manipulation.
requirements: Task boxes inserted into the device, with prompts such as time limits for task completion and auditory alarms to signal errors
constraints: The article notes skill in both groups was assessed exclusively by ArthroSim, which might have introduced a potential bias favoring the group trained on the same device
target_learners: first-year medical students without prior surgical training
target_learning_goals: basic arthroscopic inspection, instrument handling, and object manipulation skills
examples: Participants were instructed to complete the 8-task boxes in sequential order, repeating tasks as time allowed during the 90-minute session
